Subject: Observability: prioritization for per-route economics & anomaly alerts

Hi team,

Following up from our product sync — Vertex is seeing intermittent tenant spillover where cost jumps on one route cause latency regressions on adjacent routes. They asked for two console features that would help both sides:

1) A per-route "spillover matrix" view that shows correlated cost & latency spikes across routes over a sliding 24h window (heatmap + top contributing tenants).
2) Alerting that triggers when per-route token-cost per minute increases > X% while tail latency for related routes also increases > Y% (configurable thresholds).

Marcus — can you confirm feasibility and rough engineering effort (sprint points)? Aditya — would this require new ingestion metrics or can we reuse the existing per-token cost counters + route tags? Naomi & Lauren — want your input on prioritization and whether this should be an SLO-tied feature or a product analytics widget.

I've attached a small sample CSV from Vertex (route-sample.csv) illustrating a day where the spillover pattern showed up. Cindy from Vertex is copied.

Goal: decide scope for a v1 that we can aim to include in the Observability sprint starting Apr 10.

Thanks,

--
Chloe Martin
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Vertex Analytics <ops@vertex-analytics.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability: prioritization for per-route economics & anomaly alerts

Chloe,

Thanks for the context and the CSV — useful. Short answers first: feasible; we can ship a scoped v1 in ~3 sprint-weeks with a small team if we limit the initial surface. Notes: 

- Ingestion: we can reuse per-token cost counters + existing route tags (no schema changes). However, to compute the spillover correlation efficiently we should pre-aggregate by 1-minute buckets and materialize a small moving window. That will add ~1 CPU/GPU cost for the ingestion job at peak.
- UI: v1 can be a heatmap matrix with per-cell drilldown showing top 5 contributing tenants and the token-pathway (sequence of routes that requests hit).
- Alerts: the alerting engine can use existing rules but needs a new composite condition (cost delta AND tail latency delta). That is ~2 days for rule plumbing + 3 days for testing + 2 for rollout.

Questions for product:
- What thresholds are acceptable for X% (cost) and Y% (latency)? Do we want static defaults or dynamic/auto thresholds (e.g., 3-sigma)?
- Do we want to tie alerts to SLOs (so they generate escalation paths) or keep them as informatory metrics for now?

I'll draft an engineering estimate doc this afternoon and post to RED-4521.

Thanks for the signal and Marcus for the estimate. A few product-side proposals to help scope v1: 

- MVP surface: (A) Spillover matrix heatmap (24h) with cell-level top-tenant list, (B) Composite alert with default thresholds: cost +50% over baseline and p95 latency +30% (configurable), (C) One-click runbook link that creates a triage task with prefilled context.
- SLO: recommend NOT tying to formal SLOs initially. Keep as operational alerts (pager optional) and evaluate after 30 days of telemetry.
- UX: expose an optional "route-group" filter so customers can group related routes (helps reduce noise).

Action items:
1) Marcus: post engineering estimate to RED-4521 by EOD Wed (29 Mar).
2) Chloe: draft PRD v1 and share link.
3) Aditya: confirm ingestion cost estimate and whether we need a small retention bump for per-minute aggregates.
